groups.name: Medicines that prolong the QT interval

src.q: Prolongation of the QT interval, reflecting effects on cardiac repolarisation imparting a risk of developing cardiac arrhythmia and torsades de pointes , have been seen in patients treated with macrolides including clarithromycin
Ciprofloxacin and moxifloxacin increase the QTc by less than 10 ms in most cases.
Hepatic dysfunction, including increased liver enzymes, and hepatocellular and/or cholestatic hepatitis, with or without jaundice, has been reported with clarithromycin.
Cases of fatal hepatic failure (see section 4.8) have been reported.
Cases of hepatic necrosis and life-threatening hepatic failure have been reported with ciprofloxacin
Hepatic events may be severe and in extremely rare circumstances, deaths have been reported.

notes: Batch E (amoxicillin, co-amoxiclav, clarithromycin, ciprofloxacin). BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). emc search for co-amoxiclav/clarithromycin/ciprofloxacin returned no results from here, so SmPCs were found via emc 'browse active ingredient' pages. Klaricid (originator clarithromycin) and Ciproxin tablets were not listed on emc; mainstream generics were used (Milpharm clarithromycin tablets, Ranbaxy clarithromycin suspension, Ranbaxy ciprofloxacin tablets) plus Bayer Ciproxin suspension and GSK Augmentin SmPCs. An older Ranbaxy clarithromycin 500 mg tablet SmPC (emc 4357) gives only 500 mg twice daily 'in severe infections' and was not used; the Milpharm SmPC gives 250 mg twice daily usual dose. CONFLICTS: (1) Pregnancy: co-amoxiclav SmPC says use should be avoided unless considered essential, ciprofloxacin SmPCs say preferable to avoid / not recommended, clarithromycin SmPC says not advised without weighing benefit and risk, whereas BUMPS leaflets say each can be used/taken in pregnancy if recommended by a doctor. Both are recorded as separate items. (2) Breastfeeding: amoxicillin/co-amoxiclav SmPCs say use only after benefit/risk assessment, SPS says all penicillins can be used with precautionary infant monitoring; clarithromycin SmPC says safety not established, SPS says can be used with precautionary infant monitoring. No SPS quinolone breastfeeding page was found (searched; candidate URLs returned 404), so ciprofloxacin breastfeeding relies on the SmPCs only. (3) Clarithromycin + severe hepatic failure with renal impairment: the immediate-release tablet and suspension SmPCs list it in section 4.3 with 'should not be used' wording, the Xetinin XL SmPC says 'is contraindicated'; rule level set to contraindicated because both place it in section 4.3. (4) Clarithromycin + atorvastatin: SmPC only says caution with statins other than simvastatin/lovastatin; SPS says avoid and use max 20 mg atorvastatin daily if unavoidable; MHRA DSU says do not exceed 20 mg. Recorded as an 'avoid' rule from SPS/MHRA plus a separate SmPC 'caution' statin-group rule. (5) Ciprofloxacin renal table: tablet SmPC uses '<=30' while Ciproxin suspension uses '< 30' (mL/min/1.73 m2, labelled creatinine clearance). (6) Clarithromycin paediatric suspension renal threshold is given as creatinine clearance in ml/min/1.73 m2 (encoded as CrCl). NOT FOUND in accessed UK sources: any NSAID-ciprofloxacin seizure interaction (absent from both ciprofloxacin SmPCs used); a statement that co-amoxiclav strengths are 'not interchangeable' (SmPCs instead say to choose another presentation to avoid unnecessarily high clavulanic acid doses, and that 250/125 tablets are not recommended in children < 40 kg); age bands for the co-amoxiclav suspension 'NR - Not recommended' table (the table did not render in page text). The 2019 MHRA fluoroquinolone DSU is marked superseded by the January 2024 DSU, so only the 2024 article is cited. Group memberships for statin, oral-antidiabetic, corticosteroid, calcium-channel-blocker, iron/calcium/magnesium preparations and antacids are expected from batches C, D and G; rules here reference those groups. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent second check, see audit/E.md): renal boundaries corrected (amoxicillin GFR 10 to 30 and co-amoxiclav CrCl 10-30 now include 30; clarithromycin XL and ciprofloxacin 30-60 bands now include 60; ciprofloxacin <=30 vs <30 split into tablet and suspension rules). Amoxicillin product-specific rules (renal, hepatic, pregnancy, breastfeeding, infectious mononucleosis, warfarin, methotrexate) are now limited to amoxicillin formulations, because the engine applies a rule whose med is an ingredient id to every medicine containing that ingredient (so they were also firing for co-amoxiclav, e.g. amoxicillin renal doses for 875/125 tablets). The co-amoxiclav suspension NR table is a weight-based dose-volume image (not an age table): for the 4:1 suspension the 60 mg/15 mg/kg/day dose is NR at low body weights; it cannot be quoted because it is an image, and the engine has no weight rule. Excipient rules now also use batch G condition hereditary-sugar-intolerance (glucose-galactose malabsorption etc.); the batch E condition hereditary-fructose-intolerance is now named for fructose intolerance only. Groups carbapenem and monobactam (no master-list members) added only so these allergies can be recorded against the beta-lactam cross-reactivity contraindication.
